title: I was doing (past continuous) and I did (past simple)
subtitle: I was reading / I read
summary: Use the past continuous for the longer, unfinished action and the past simple for the short, complete action.

lesson.heading: Jack and the phone
lesson.text: Jack was reading a book. Then the phone rang. He stopped reading and answered the phone. What **happened**? The phone **rang**. What **was** Jack **doing** when the phone rang? He **was reading** a book. What **did** he **do** when the phone rang? He **stopped** reading and **answered** the phone.

examples.note: past simple - a short, finished action

lesson.heading: Which action started first?
lesson.text: Jack began reading *before* the phone rang. So *when* the phone rang, he **was reading**. The reading started first and was not finished. The phone call came in the middle of it.

examples.text: Jack **was reading** a book **when** the phone **rang**.

examples.note: = it started raining before we went out

lesson.heading: Three questions about the same story

left.label: past simple: we played (complete action)
left.text: *A:* What **did** you **do** yesterday morning? *B:* We **played** tennis. (from 10 to 11.30)
examples: Jack **read** a book yesterday. (= from beginning to end)
**Did** you **watch** the film on television last night?
**It didn't rain** while we were on holiday.

right.label: past continuous: we were playing (unfinished action)
right.text: *A:* What **were** you **doing** at 10.30? *B:* We **were playing** tennis.
examples: Jack **was reading** a book when the phone rang.
**Were** you **watching** television when I phoned you?
**It wasn't raining** when I got up.

lesson.heading: More examples
lesson.text: The past simple gives us the whole action from start to finish. The past continuous puts us in the middle of the action.

examples.text: I **started** work at 9 o'clock and **finished** at 4.30. At 2.30 **I was working**.
I **saw** Lucy and Steve this morning. They **were waiting** at the bus stop.
Yesterday Sue **was walking** along the road when she **met** James.

lesson.text: The long action takes was/were + -ing; the short action that comes in the middle takes the past simple: *Kelly **fell** asleep while she **was reading**.*

exercises.prompt: Lucy broke her arm last week. It ___ when she was painting her room.
exercises.explanation: A short, finished action: it happened (past simple).

exercises.prompt: 'Was Jane busy when you went to see her?' 'Yes, she ___.'
exercises.explanation: She was in the middle of studying, so: she was studying.

exercises.prompt: Jack ___ a book when the phone rang.
exercises.explanation: The reading started before the phone call, so the longer action takes the past continuous.

exercises.prompt: The train ___ at the station and Paula got off.
exercises.explanation: A short, complete action: the train arrived.

exercises.prompt: Paula got off the train. Her friends Jon and Rachel ___ to meet her.
exercises.explanation: They started waiting before she arrived: they were waiting.

exercises.prompt: You want to know about the post this morning. Ask the question.
exercises.answer: What time did the post arrive this morning?
exercises.explanation: Past simple question: did + subject + verb.
The breakfast was the longer action: while I was having breakfast.

exercises.prompt: Is the action complete (past simple) or unfinished (past continuous)?

items.text: Jack was reading when the phone rang.
It didn't rain while we were on holiday.
It wasn't raining when I got up.

exercises.statement: Kelly fell asleep while she was reading.
exercises.explanation: Correct. The short action (fell asleep) is past simple; the long action (was reading) is past continuous.

exercises.statement: I saw Lucy and Steve this morning. They waited at the bus stop.
exercises.explanation: They were waiting at the bus stop. They started waiting before I saw them.

exercises.prompt: 'How fast ___ when the police stopped you?' 'I'm not sure, but I wasn't driving very fast.'
exercises.explanation: The driving was in progress when the police stopped you: were you driving.

exercises.prompt: 'How did you break the window?' 'We were playing football. I kicked the ball and it ___ the window.'
exercises.explanation: A short, complete action: it hit the window (past simple).
